Herbicides and natural compounds

Seven toxicity endpoints, molecular traits, and the evidence behind them A descriptive comparison of the project’s curated selection. Prepared 2026-10-22 from cached PubChem and EPA evidence. This selection is purposive; the plots describe these compounds.

data.text/markdown:
1 · Toxicity evidence across seven endpoints

These are distributions of evidence availability, rather than distributions of toxicity doses. Each bar retains every selected compound in that group. A missing record or unassessed source is never evidence that a chemical is safe.

Reading the gaps: NOAEL and LOAEL add substantial chronic evidence. BMD is absent in this cache and BMDL is sparse. EPA requires an explicit experimental source mark; BMD/BMDL are model-derived points of departure from those data. Stored TEST predictions remain separate. PubChem prose extraction is acute-only, so its chronic zeros describe an extraction limitation. Gray segments include unresolved identities and sources not assessed. The union is unknown when neither source is positive and one is unassessed. These flags do not establish absence of evidence outside the cached sources.

data.text/markdown:
2 · The groups differ in chemistry as well as evidence

The default view shows boxplots with one point per compound. Boxes span the middle 50%, with a median line and whiskers reaching the most extreme observations within 1.5 interquartile ranges. Points include outliers; their vertical spread only separates overlapping compounds. Hover for names and group sample sizes. Missing and nonfinite values are excluded. Switch to Cumulative distributions to compare whole distributions, normalized within group: at a given x-value, the curve gives the fraction at or below that value. In this selection, median molecular weight is 275.7 vs 174.7 g/mol, and median XLogP is 2.7 vs 1.7 (herbicides, then natural compounds). The curves overlap; neither property alone is a toxicity or safety score.

What to take forward

The project now supports all seven endpoint types, but evidence is uneven. NOAEL/LOAEL expand chronic availability; BMD/BMDL still need more data and study context. Molecular distributions differ in this selection, while evidence-availability models often remain close to simple baselines. A next analysis should match study context for chronic potency and match ToxCast panels before interpreting activity differences. Neither missing data nor a classifier label establishes safety. Reproducibility: prepared products in data/ are verified against manifest.json before display. The manifest records source and code hashes; source caches and generated products remain local. This snapshot used 8 comparison policies (seven types plus the trout-specific LC50 policy). See analysis/README.md for rebuild and export commands.
